entry.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
entry.summary:
Remark: This work is in submission at STOC'27 and thus the full manuscript has been publicly posted on the conference website since November 3rd, 2026. Inspired by the Codeword-Hash Structure problem recently introduced by Cakan (arXiV, 2026) to separate $\mathsf{QMA}$ from $\mathsf{QCIP}$, we introduce a new problem called Codeword-Hash pairs in Noise ($\mathsf{CHN}$) and prove that, in the query complexity model, it is in $\mathsf{QMA}$ but hard for the $\mathsf{QCMA}$ hierarchy $\mathsf{QCMAH} = \bigcup_{d\geq1}\mathsf{QCMA}^{\mathsf{QCMA}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{QCMA}}}}$, the classical-witness quantum-verifier analogue of $\mathsf{PH}=\bigcup_{d\ge1}\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{NP}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{NP}}}}$. Using this problem, we show that there exists a classical oracle ${O}$ such that $\mathsf{P}^{O}=\mathsf{BQP}^{O}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{O} =\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O} \subset \mathsf{QMA}^{O} \text{ but } \mathsf{QMA}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O},$ thus showing that quantum state or quantum proof advantage could exist even if classical computers can efficiently solve any problem that can be quantumly verified with a classical proof.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #cryptography #combinatorics

entry.title: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
entry.summary:
As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. In practice, users pursue legitimate goals through multi-turn, multimodal interactions, where seemingly benign requests may become safety-critical when considered alongside earlier actions and visual observations.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Modular Walsh rigidity for Boolean functions of degree at most four
entry.summary:
We establish the sufficient ratio $p/2^m \ge 1/2$ for Boolean functions of algebraic degree at most four in $4m$ variables for every $m \ge 4$. The modulus $p$ is odd and may be composite. If every unnormalized Walsh coefficient is congruent to one of the two bent levels modulo $p$, the function is bent.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Rich Input Representations in Neural Differential Cryptanalysis: A Taxonomy and Survey
entry.summary:
Neural differential distinguishers have become an active research direction in​ symmetric-key cryptanalysis since the introduction of deep-learning-based attacks on​ round-reduced SPECK. Early neural distinguishers typically used a single ciphertext pair​ or ciphertext difference as input. Recent studies, however, show that richer input​ representations can substantially affect the information available to the classifier, the data​ cost of each labeled sample, and the relevance of the distinguisher to practical attacks.​ Examples include multi-pair, multi-difference, matrix-style, multi-round,​ structured-encoding, and score-aggregation based inputs.​ This paper provides a taxonomy and survey of rich input representations in neural​ differential cryptanalysis.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #neuroscience

entry.title: Symphony: Scalable SNARKs in the Random Oracle Model from Lattice-Based High-Arity Folding
entry.summary:
Folding/Accumulation schemes are a powerful tool for building scalable proof systems. However, standard approaches for leveraging folding schemes, such as IVCs or PCDs, require embedding hash functions (modeled as random oracles) into recursive circuits, introducing both security concerns and significant proving overhead. We re-envision how to use folding schemes, and introduce Symphony, the first proving paradigm that leverages folding schemes as a black box without embedding hashes in SNARK circuits.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #post-quantum

entry.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function. The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$.
entry.summary:
The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory

entry.title: Optimized G+G Signature
entry.summary:
At ASIACRYPT 2023, Devevey, Passelègue, and Stehlé introduced the G+G signature, a Fiat–Shamir lattice signature based on Gaussian convolution that avoids rejection sampling during signing. Although G+G achieves competitive signature sizes, its spherical Gaussian response distribution leaves room for further optimization. In this work, we propose an optimized G+G signature by incorporating asymmetric secret-key distributions into key generation and introducing a three-block non-spherical Gaussian response distribution.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Homomorphic NIZKs and Maliciously-Secure MPC with Optimal Communication Complexity from Standard Assumptions
entry.summary:
We construct fully-homomorphic NIZKs and a communication-complexity-preserving semi-malicious to malicious multiparty computation (MPC) compiler from a broader range of cryptographic assumptions, including $\mathsf{LWE}$, $O(1)$-$\mathsf{LIN}$, and $\mathsf{DDH}$ (without circular security assumptions). Prior to this work, homomorphic NIZKs were only known based on pairing-based techniques while prior MPC compilers with similar efficiency required strong non-falsifiable assumptions. A key ingredient that we develop in this work is a new notion of a partially-hiding succinct delegation system, that we call encrypted RAM (eRAM) delegation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #combinatorics
